column1: # Camera treatment per narration segment. Tab-separated: seg <TAB> phases
# The camera is either perfectly still or moving deliberately — never drifting. An earlier cut
# panned slowly through every shot to avoid dead air; it read as a constant shake with text sliding
# off screen. Stillness is correct: the UI's own motion (rows landing, the event stream, the replay)
# is what keeps a held shot alive.
# phases: semicolon-separated, each `kind:seconds[:X,Y,W,H]` in MASTER coords (3200x1800).
#   full          whole frame, pixel-locked
#   hl            whole frame, pixel-locked, with an accent border around the region about to be
#                 discussed. Always precedes a zoom so the eye arrives before the camera does.
#   zin           ~1s eased move from whole frame to the target rect
#   hold          locked on the target rect, zero drift
#   zout          ~1s eased move from the target rect back to the whole frame
#   sp            split screen: the rect fills the 1120x1080 left pane, pixel-locked for the whole
#                 segment, while the panel beside it animates. `pre` means the clip is already
#                 framed for the left pane. The seconds field is ignored — a split segment is one
#                 locked hold that lasts exactly as long as its narration.
# A zoom target must be 16:9 or it will letterbox; a highlight rect can be any shape; an sp rect
# must match the left pane's 1120:1080 shape or the build refuses it rather than stretching the UI.
# The final phase's duration is computed to make the segment match its narration exactly, so the
# numbers below are the fixed ones and the last phase absorbs the remainder.
